paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Диаграмата представя сравнение на перплексността при два типа прунинг — „Per-Output“ и „Per-Layer“ — за различни нива на разреждане (sparsity rate), изразени като проценти от 10% до 80%, като по вертикалната ос е използвана логаритмична скала, обхващаща диапазона от 10¹ до 10³. По хоризонталната ос са разположени категориите „Sparsity Rate“ в нарастващ ред, като всяка стойност е представена с два стълба — син за „Per-Output“ и оранжев за „Per-Layer“. Всички стълбове са подредени по нарастващо ниво на разреждане, без допълнително подчертаване на отделни стойности. При ниски нива на разреждане (до 50%) височините на стълбовете за двете конфигурации са почти идентични, като перплексността остава под 10¹. При 60% разреждане синият стълб (Per-Output) достига стойност около 15, докато оранжевият (Per-Layer) остава близо до 10¹. При 70% разреждане разликата се увеличава — Per-Output достига около 50, а Per-Layer — около 25. При 80% разреждане и двете стойности се приближават към 10³, като синият стълб остава леко по-висок от оранжевия.
model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart compares the perplexity of two pruning strategies—“Per-Output” and “Per-Layer”—across eight increasing sparsity rates (10% to 80%) in large language models, with values plotted on a logarithmic y-axis ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The horizontal x-axis lists sparsity rates in 10% increments, ordered from left to right, while the vertical y-axis, labeled “Perplexity,” uses a base-10 logarithmic scale with major gridlines at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. Each sparsity rate is represented by a pair of adjacent bars: blue for “Per-Output” and orange for “Per-Layer,” as indicated by the legend in the upper left. At lower sparsity rates (10% to 50%), both configurations show nearly identical perplexity values, all remaining below 10^1. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar rises to approximately 15, while the Per-Layer bar stays near 10. At 70%, the divergence becomes more pronounced, with Per-Output reaching roughly 50 and Per-Layer approximately 25. At the highest sparsity rate of 80%, both bars approach 10^3, with the Per-Output bar slightly taller than the Per-Layer bar, indicating marginally higher perplexity. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, outlines, or annotations beyond their color coding and positioning. The chart visually conveys that both pruning methods perform similarly up to 50% sparsity, after which Per-Output degradation accelerates relative to Per-Layer, particularly at 70% and 80% sparsity.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates a comparison of perplexity values for two pruning strategies—“Per-Output” (blue bars) and “Per-Layer” (orange bars)—across increasing sparsity rates from 10% to 80%, with the y-axis representing perplexity on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^3. The x-axis lists sparsity rates in 10% increments, and for each rate, two adjacent bars show the respective perplexity for each pruning method. At sparsity rates of 10% through 50%, both configurations exhibit perplexity values below 10^1, appearing visually similar and clustered near the bottom of the chart. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output bar rises to approximately 15 while the Per-Layer bar remains close to 10^1 (~10). The divergence becomes more pronounced at 70% sparsity, where Per-Output reaches roughly 50 and Per-Layer approximately 25. At the highest sparsity of 80%, both bars approach 10^3, with the Per-Output bar slightly taller than the Per-Layer bar, indicating marginally higher perplexity. The chart visually confirms that while both methods perform similarly at moderate sparsity, Per-Output degrades more rapidly as sparsity increases beyond 50%.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm vergleicht die Perplexität zweier Pruning-Strategien — „Per-Output“ (blau) und „Per-Layer“ (orange) — bei unterschiedlichen Sparsitätsraten (10 % bis 80 %), wobei die Perplexität auf einer logarithmischen y-Achse dargestellt ist, die von 10¹ bis 10³ reicht und mit Tick-Markierungen bei 10¹, 10² und 10³ skaliert ist; die x-Achse zeigt die Sparsitätsrate in 10 %-Schritten, beschriftet mit „10%“ bis „80%“. Jede Sparsitätsrate ist durch ein Paar nebeneinander angeordneter Balken repräsentiert, wobei der linke Balken „Per-Output“ und der rechte „Per-Layer“ entspricht. Bei Sparsitätsraten von 10 % bis 50 % liegen beide Balken nahe bei 10¹, was auf vergleichbare Perplexitätswerte hindeutet. Ab 60 % steigt der „Per-Output“-Balken auf etwa 15, während der „Per-Layer“-Balken bei etwa 10¹ verbleibt. Bei 70 % erreicht „Per-Output“ etwa 50 und „Per-Layer“ etwa 25. Bei 80 % nähern sich beide Balken dem Wert 10³, wobei der „Per-Output“-Balken leicht höher ist als der „Per-Layer“-Balken. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern nach steigender Sparsitätsrate angeordnet, und keine Balken sind visuell hervorgehoben; die Legende oben links identifiziert die Farben der beiden Konfigurationen.
